newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere says DASA link helps build Europe - paper.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere says DASA link helps build Europe - paper.

text.p: France's Lagardere Groupe said on Thursday its controversial plan to link up with Germany's DASA aerospace firm was far from being an opportunistic move and represented a strengthening of the European defence industry.

Missiles-to-books group Lagardere, as part of its bid in the privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, has struck far-reaching cooperation agreements with Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) in space, missiles and electronics.

"Our alliance with the Germans was in the natural order of things as we have a number of cooperative programmes. Our European alliances are anything but alliances of chance," Lagardere managing director Noel Forgeard told newspaper le Figaro in an interview.
That alliance sparked an attack from rival French bidder engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom this week which said the Lagardere deal would lead to a break-up of Thomson-CSF.

And the chairman of state-owned Aerospatiale, Yves Michot, warned that a Lagardere-DASA link-up threatened the Airbus Industrie passenger jet consortium, in which Aerospatiale is a senior partner with DASA.

Lagardere said two years ago at the last Paris air show that it wanted to ally with DASA but the time had not been ripe then, Forgeard said. "Today, DASA is convinced that we are a defining moment in the building of Europe and that our agreement can accelerate it," Forgeard said.
"These alliances are independent of Thomson-CSF as they will go ahead, in any case, with or without Thomson," he said.

The link up with DASA also helped ensure the German firm stayed in the European fold as a third of its turnover came from cooperative deals in the United States and had been considering teaming up with a U.S. satellite observation project, he said.

Foregeard denied claims made by Alcatel that Lagardere had made concessions to DASA which endangered French sovereignty and said DASA had chosen Lagardere as the strongest partner in the European space industry.

Armand Carlier, chairman of Lagardere's Matra Marconi Space (MMS) joint venture, said the DASA alliance would create the world's third biggest venture in the sector and by far Europe's largest. MMS is jointly owned by Britain's GEC Plc.

The holdings in the enlarged space group would reflect the assets vested in it, following a valutaion process, but the shareholding would be "favourable" to MMS, which would continue to hold a majority. Carlier would be the chairman of the management board and a German would head the supervisory board, Forgeard said.
Thomson-CSF's cash would ensure the future growth of Thomson-Matra, the company to be formed if Lagardere wins the bidding, he said.

Forgeard denied the DASA link threatened the missiles and space interests of Aerospatiale -- which has been courting DASA for years to form joint ventures. "We hope to make concrete proposals for cooperation with Aerospatiale. There are intelligent things to be done," he said.
He also denied the plan threatened the Airbus partnership. Aerospatiale was the leader in French aircraft manufacturing but DASA had chosen Lagardere for its defence electronics strength .

The priority on the missiles side was for the Matra BAe Dynamics missiles joint venture to cooperate with DASA on German cruise missiles and things could lead to Matra BAe taking a stake in LFK, DASA's missiles unit.
